He played [[college basketball]] for the [[James Madison Dukes men's basketball|James Madison Dukes]] and [[Dayton Flyers men's basketball|Dayton Flyers]]. ==High school career== Throughout his high school years, he played basketball at the [[Trenton Catholic Academy]] in his home state. In his junior year, he averaged 6.8 points and 0.7 rebounds per game in 23 games played there. During his senior year, he increased his production to 14.1 points and 1.0 rebounds per game in 28 games played.{{Cite web |url=http://www.highschoolsports.nj.com/player/charles-cooke/ |title=Charles Cooke Boys Basketball Bio @ Trenton Catholic High School - nj.com |access-date=August 8, 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110210184825/http://highschoolsports.nj.com/player/charles-cooke/ |archive-date=February 10, 2011 |url-status=dead }} After graduating from high school, he committed to playing for [[James Madison University]] at the [[Colonial Athletic Association]]. ==College career== In his freshman season, he averaged 5.8 points and 2.8 rebounds per game in 32 games played for the Dukes. He improved his production in his sophomore year, averaging 14.3 points, 5.0 rebounds, 1.7 assists, and 1.4 steals per game in 30 games played for James Madison. After his sophomore season, he sat out what would have originally been his junior year to transfer to the [[Dayton Flyers men's basketball|University of Dayton]] at the [[Atlantic 10 Conference]]. In his first season at Dayton, Cooke averaged 15.6 points, 5.8 rebounds, 1.8 assists, 1.3 steals, and 1.2 blocks per game in 32 games played. Finally, in his senior year, he averaged 15.8 points, 5.1 rebounds, 2.8 assists, 1.1 steals, and 1.0 blocks per game in 29 games played.{{Cite web|url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/players/charles-cooke-1.html|title = Charles Cooke College Stats}} During his time at Dayton, he became the only player to have two seasons with averages of 1 assist, 1 steal, and 1 block per game with 37.5% three-point shooting and 5 free-throw attempts per game.{{Cite web|url=https://www.thebirdwrites.com/2017/8/1/16074810/2017-nba-free-agency-charles-cooke-new-orleans-pelicans-comparisons-statistics-youtube-interview|title=New Orleans Pelicans look smart by taking a chance on Charles Cooke III|date=August 2017|access-date=August 8, 2017|archive-date=October 19, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181019155616/https://www.thebirdwrites.com/2017/8/1/16074810/2017-nba-free-agency-charles-cooke-new-orleans-pelicans-comparisons-statistics-youtube-interview|url-status=dead}} ==Professional career== While he was originally projected to be a second round pick in the [[2017 NBA draft]],{{Cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/pelicans/news/five-things-know-about-pelicans-two-way-contract-signee-charles-cooke|title=Five things to know about Pelicans two-way contract signee Charles Cooke|website=[[NBA.com]]}} he ultimately went undrafted. After the draft, he played with the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]] for the [[2017 NBA Summer League]], with the intent on signing with them afterwards.{{cite news |last=Jablonski |first=David |date=June 23, 2017 |url=http://www.daytondailynews.com/sports/dayton-charles-cooke-signs-free-agent/FBOfEzS0J4RlE1cmZwZ8YN/ |title=Dayton's Charles Cooke signs as free agent |work=Dayton Daily News |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170626010627/http://www.daytondailynews.com/sports/dayton-charles-cooke-signs-free-agent/FBOfEzS0J4RlE1cmZwZ8YN/ |archive-date=June 26, 2017}} In the five games he played for the Timberwolves, he recorded 10 points, 3 rebounds, and 1 steal per game in 20.8 minutes of action. Cooke ultimately wouldn't sign a deal with the Timberwolves.{{Cite web|url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2017/08/pelicans-charles-cooke-agree-to-two-way-deal.html|title = Pelicans Sign Charles Cooke to Two-Way Deal}} Instead, on August 2, 2017, Cooke signed a [[two-way contract]] with the [[New Orleans Pelicans]].{{cite news|title=Pelicans sign Charles Cooke to two-way contract|url=https://www.nba.com/pelicans/news/pelicans-sign-charles-cooke-two-way-contract|work=[[New Orleans Pelicans]]|date=August 2, 2017|access-date=August 2, 2017}} That meant for the majority of the season, Cooke would split his professional time between the New Orleans squad and a [[NBA G League|G-League]] affiliate that's going to be best designated to them by the league before the season begins, which turned out to be the [[Greensboro Swarm]]. He made his NBA debut on October 28, 2017, playing in two minutes and scoring two points in a blowout 123–101 win over the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]]. On October 7, 2018, Cooke signed with the [[Miami Heat]].{{cite web|title=Miami Heat sign Charles Cooke, DeAndre Liggins|url=https://www.nba.com/article/2018/10/07/miami-heat-cooke-liggins-official-release/|website=NBA.com|access-date=October 7, 2018 |date=October 7, 2018}} He was waived by the Heat on October 11 after appearing in one preseason game.{{cite web|title=Heat Signs Purvis And Putney|url=https://www.nba.com/heat/news/heat-signs-purvis-and-putney-181011|website=NBA.com|access-date=October 11, 2018|date=October 11, 2018}} Cooke was subsequently added to the roster of the [[Sioux Falls Skyforce]].{{cite web|title=SKYFORCE ANNOUNCE 2018-19 OPENING DAY ROSTER|url=https://siouxfalls.gleague.nba.com/news/skyforce-announce-2018-19-opening-day-roster/|website=NBA.com|access-date=November 6, 2018|date=November 1, 2018|archive-date=November 6, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181106093324/https://siouxfalls.gleague.nba.com/news/skyforce-announce-2018-19-opening-day-roster/|url-status=dead}} On March 15, 2019, Cooke signed a 10-day contract with the [[Miami Heat]], and was immediately assigned back to the Skyforce.{{cite web|title=HEAT Signs Charles Cooke To 10-Day Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/heat/news/heat-signs-charles-cooke-190315|website=NBA.com|access-date=March 17, 2019|date=March 15, 2019}} On August 31, 2019, [[Universo Treviso Basket|De' Longhi Treviso]] of the Italian [[Lega Basket Serie A]] (LBA),{{Cite news|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/delonghi-treviso-basket-signs-charles-cooke-iii/|title=De'Longhi Treviso Basket signs Charles
